name: Malawi
prevalence_note: MACRA's September 2026 public alert on mobile-money and WhatsApp fraud lists fake social-cash-transfer messages, forged wallet SMS followed by a demand to return money, hijacked WhatsApp accounts begging contacts for cash, and prize claims that require a payment or personal details.
cross_border_note: Messages are usually in English or Chichewa and may look like Airtel Money or TNM Mpamba system SMS, or arrive from a relative's WhatsApp after the account has been taken over.

scams.name: Fake social cash transfer payment request
scams.name_en: Fake social cash transfer payment request

red_flag_keywords.text: requires a fee before a supposed social cash transfer is paid
asks the beneficiary to send money so a grant can be released
asks the customer to confirm a benefit payment in a chat app

scams.signals_en: An ordinary SMS or WhatsApp note claims the person is due a social cash transfer or similar assistance and then asks for a payment, a wallet top-up, or personal details before the grant can be paid.
scams.legit_en: MACRA states that government bodies and civil-society groups involved in social cash transfer programmes do not use ordinary SMS or WhatsApp to ask beneficiaries for money.
bait_tactics: I am not sending Mpamba or Airtel Money to release a grant that arrived as an ordinary WhatsApp note.
No official programme I already use has told me, through its usual channel, that a fee is due today.
This handset shows no pending official assistance payment in the wallet history.

scams.name: Forged mobile-money SMS and refund demand
scams.name_en: Forged mobile-money SMS and refund demand
context_keywords: money has been sent to you

red_flag_keywords.text: treats a look-alike wallet SMS as proof of a credit and demands a refund
claims a payment platform failed and gives a different destination number
discourages checking the official balance before reversing a supposed credit

scams.signals_en: A message is styled like a genuine Airtel Money or TNM Mpamba credit alert, or claims a payment platform has failed, and the sender then demands an immediate transfer to another number.
scams.legit_en: MACRA tells the public not to return money solely on the basis of an SMS that claims funds were sent, and to confirm the transaction through the proper mobile-money platform or the account balance first.
bait_tactics: The official Mpamba balance on this phone has not gone up, so I am not sending a refund from my own wallet.
I will not treat a message that merely looks like a system SMS as proof of a deposit.
There is no record in this Airtel Money history of the credit you are describing.

scams.name: Hijacked WhatsApp or unexpected prize claim
scams.name_en: Hijacked WhatsApp or unexpected prize claim

red_flag_keywords.text: uses a known contact's chat account to ask for money on a new number
announces an unexpected prize and requires a payment to collect it
asks funds to be sent to a different wallet while claiming the chat is still genuine

scams.signals_en: Either a known contact's WhatsApp, after the account has been taken over, asks friends and family for money, or an unexpected prize message demands a payment or personal data before winnings can be collected.
scams.legit_en: MACRA warns about compromised WhatsApp accounts used to solicit money, and says that if someone did not enter a competition they cannot win its prize. Requests should be verified through a usual telephone number or a trusted person.
bait_tactics: I am not sending money from a WhatsApp chat until I have reached this person on the number I already use for them.
I did not enter any prize draw on this line, so I will not pay a collection charge.
The tone of this message is not how that relative usually asks me for help.
